summary: Executed the two gating phases of plan 04 (Gate A variant selection, Gate B persistence prototype), in the order the plan itself specifies for a single-dispatch scenario (Gate B first, since it is the option-killer). Both gates returned PASS verdicts. Gate A: re-ran task 574's variant-selection methodology against the current (post-574, post-585) tree; both V1 (self-copy reinstated verbatim) and V4 (generalized to copy every positive formula) saturate identically to the control (len=219, maxLabel=21, matching 574's own recorded measurement) at fuel>=120, stable through fuel=200, with all 20 propositional conformance rows matching for both. V4 selected (higher-value target, and this empirically retires the plan's flagged 'V4 might diverge' risk). Gate B: prototyped the single loop-back hop persistence question in scratch/PersistPrototype.lean (lake env lean verified against real library types). Verdict PASS (conditional) -- not refuted, unlike the quotient route which has a concrete counterexample. The descendant sub-case closes cleanly; the ancestor sub-case needs origin-tracing, which is not a fresh problem -- it is a repurposing of Scheme.lean's already-landed private IWorldHist provenance machinery (par/obl/fire/sfor witness functions, built by task 585 for DP-2). Zero writes to Cslib/ or CslibTests/ (both gates are scratch-only per the plan's explicit constraint). Phases 3-8 (revert a70187dd in V4-generalized form, fixpoint completeness, invariant threading, and the three sorry discharges) remain and were not attempted in this dispatch -- the plan itself estimates the two gates alone at ~2 dispatches, and phases 3-8 are deliberately not given a firm budget.
